process_stages.description: Candidate-report compilation: recruiter screen, CodeSignal online assessment, technical phone screen, then a four-round virtual onsite (two coding, system design, values), followed by a hiring-committee decision.

interview_styles.statement: Practical building over puzzles: extending/working in a real codebase, concurrency and transaction reasoning, system design with quantitative estimates, and values/velocity behavioral questions.

thesis_text:
Bottom line: for Ramp (Software Engineering (SWE), entry), your odds through the cold application alone are low, but not zero. This read rests on a curated-qualitative record as of 2026-10-12 with no population sample — treat every pattern below as reported, not measured. Builder bar: Ramp's official page says it only hires builders and frames its founding hiring test in founder-like terms; candidate reports describe practical system-building assessments. No pass rate is published in fetched sources.

Who gets in (sample N=not available — curated-qualitative record, as of 2026-10-12):
- A secondary JD analysis in the internship guide lists Python as the dominant backend langu — reported pattern, not a measured share: A secondary JD analysis in the internship guide lists Python as the dominant backend language in Ramp intern descriptions, with TypeScript/React on the frontend and SQL/PostgreSQL recurring. (source: https://www.extern.com/post/ramp-internship-guide, as of 2026-10-12)
- Candidate-report compilation describes the assessment emphasis as building a working syste — reported pattern, not a measured share: Candidate-report compilation describes the assessment emphasis as building a working system (progressive levels) rather than isolated algorithmic puzzles. (source: https://github.com/landedjobs/ai-interview-guides/blob/HEAD/guides/ramp.md, as of 2026-10-12)
- Ramp's own careers page frames the hiring identity as builders who ship, across functions. — reported pattern, not a measured share: Ramp's own careers page frames the hiring identity as builders who ship, across functions. (source: https://ramp.com/careers?utm_id=1641699&utm_source=Business+Job+Board, as of 2026-10-12)
Known biases of this data: Survivorship bias: candidate-report guides reflect people who interviewed, disproportionately those who progressed.; Secondary-source risk: intern posting dates/pay come from a guide summarizing Ashby postings, not from a fetched Ashby posting body (the Ashby page renders via JavaScript and returned no posting text when fetched).; Official careers page is deliberately provocative employer marketing; treat its culture claims as stated, not revealed, preference.; No H-1B LCA, university-outcome or licensed population data was fetched in this pass.. We see who got in, not who tried and failed — survivorship bias is real (§0).
